map.基于 Cariogram 模型的龋病风险多因素评估。综合 7 项临床因素，判断未: Multi-factor caries risk assessment based on the Cariogram model. It combines 7 clinical factors to judge the risk of new caries and helps build a personalized prevention plan.
map.高龋患者录入饮食、菌群、氟暴露等七因素，工具输出风险等级与主要可控因素。: For high-caries-risk patients, enter seven factors such as diet, flora and fluoride exposure; the tool outputs the risk level and the main controllable factors.
map.儿童防龋随访，提示加强局部用氟与饮食控糖的重点。: For children's caries prevention follow-ups, it highlights the key points of strengthening local fluoride use and controlling dietary sugar.
map.正畸期间复评风险，关注托槽周围清洁难度。（结果仅供口腔健康科普与自我初筛参考，不: Re-assess the risk during orthodontic treatment and pay attention to cleaning difficulty around brackets. (Results are for oral-health education and self-screening reference only, and do not replace dental examinations, periapical radiographs or CBCT imaging, nor diagnosis and treatment by a dentist, orthodontist or periodontist; if you have tooth pain, bleeding gums, ulcers that will not heal, abnormal oral mucosa or occlusal discomfort, see a dental department of a proper hospital promptly.)
map.：输入：7 因素（高糖摄入、变异链球菌高、氟低、唾液少…）\n输出：高风险，主要:
Input: 7 factors (high sugar intake, high mutans streptococci, low fluoride, low salivary flow...)
Output: high risk, main controllable factors = diet and fluoride exposure; recommend fluoride, sealants, sugar control and a 3~6 month recheck.

map.常用维度含龋病经历、饮食（糖）、菌群（变链）、氟、唾液缓冲/流率、社会因素与既往: Common dimensions include caries history, diet (sugar), flora (mutans streptococci), fluoride, salivary buffering and flow, social factors and past restorations, combined into a weighted risk score.
map.高风险意味着什么？: What Does a High Risk Level Mean?
map.未来 1~2 年新龋概率高，应强化防龋（专业涂氟、窝沟封闭、饮食管理）并缩短复查: A high probability of new caries in the next 1-2 years calls for stronger prevention (professional fluoride, fissure sealing, diet management) and shorter review intervals.
map.评分能代替口腔检查吗？: Can the Score Replace a Dental Exam?
map.不能。本工具为风险评估辅助，方案与确诊以口腔医师检查为准；有活跃龋及时就诊。: No. This tool is a risk-assessment aid; the plan and the diagnosis must come from a dentist's examination. See a dentist promptly if there is active caries.
